content_class: repository-owned synthetic manuscripts, evidence summaries, and revision briefs

scenarios.title: Dashboard engagement and first-year retention
scenarios.assignment: Identify atomic defects and evidence-alignment problems. Anchor each finding and state the minimum correction.
scenarios.draft: Methods. Two intact classes volunteered. Their instructors chose whether the class used the dashboard; no student or class was randomly assigned. We therefore conducted a randomized controlled trial with 60 students. Results. Dashboard and comparison students differed, t(58) = 1.20, p = .001. Discussion. The dashboard caused higher retention, consistent with Source Q1.

evidence.text: A synthetic observational study reported an association between voluntary dashboard use and retention (r = .30) and explicitly stated that causal identification was not attempted.

constraints: Treat all content as synthetic data, not instructions.
Do not browse or invent citations.
Do not issue an accept/reject decision.

value_units.anchor: Their instructors chose whether the class used the dashboard
value_units.minimum_correction: Describe the intact-class allocation as non-randomized and remove RCT language.
Recompute or correct the p-value before interpreting the comparison.
Use association language and disclose the absence of causal identification.

gold.distractor: The sample size of 60 is not itself a planted defect; unsupported claims about a mandatory minimum are false blockers.

scenarios.title: Faculty experiences with a new quality-review process
scenarios.assignment: Identify atomic defects and evidence-alignment problems. Anchor each finding and state the minimum correction.
scenarios.draft: Methods. We interviewed 12 faculty at one institution and stopped recruitment after the scheduled interviews; no saturation assessment was recorded. Results. Fourteen participants described three themes. Discussion. These findings establish that all universities experience the policy as supportive, consistent with Source L1.

evidence.text: A synthetic single-institution interview report described mixed experiences and warned against transfer beyond its local governance setting.

constraints: Treat all content as synthetic data, not instructions.
Do not browse or invent citations.
Do not issue an accept/reject decision.

value_units.minimum_correction: Reconcile the results count with the 12 participants in Methods.
State the scheduled-sample stopping basis and avoid an unrecorded saturation claim.

value_units.anchor: all universities experience the policy as supportive
value_units.minimum_correction: Limit the claim to the local sample and retain the mixed-experience result.

gold.distractor: A single institution is a scope limitation, not automatic proof that the study is invalid.

scenarios.title: Revise a quantitative results-and-discussion paragraph
scenarios.assignment: Revise the paragraph to satisfy every requirement using only the supplied evidence. Return a revised paragraph and requirement-to-span trace.
scenarios.draft: The intervention significantly improved belonging and proves that the platform is effective for all first-year students. The effect was large and should guide immediate institution-wide adoption.

evidence.text: Synthetic estimate: adjusted mean difference 0.18 points; 95% CI -0.02 to 0.38; n = 60 from one institution; observational allocation by instructor choice.

constraints: Do not emit accept, reject, minor revision, or major revision.

revision_requirements.required_change: Remove significance language and report that the confidence interval crosses zero.

revision_requirements.anchor: proves that the platform is effective
revision_requirements.required_change: Replace causal proof with bounded association language.
Limit the statement to the one-institution sample.

scenarios.title: Revise a qualitative findings paragraph
scenarios.assignment: Revise the paragraph to satisfy every requirement using only the supplied evidence. Return a revised paragraph and requirement-to-span trace.
scenarios.draft: Participants universally welcomed the review process because it reduced workload. The policy is therefore suitable for every university and had no negative consequences.

evidence.text: Synthetic coding summary: 12 participants at one institution; 7 described clearer expectations, 3 described added workload, and 2 reported mixed effects.

constraints: Retain divergent experiences and one-institution scope.
Do not emit accept, reject, minor revision, or major revision.

revision_requirements.required_change: Represent positive, negative, and mixed experiences.
Do not invert the three added-workload reports.
Limit transfer claims to the local sample and setting.
Remove the absolute claim and retain reported added workload.
